verdict: The Uruk Rumble is FrizzleBob's Mesopotamian masterpiece — Gilgamesh as wrestling event, Humbaba as the Jobber, Tablet XII as the Retcon, Mayfly Philosophy as the best existential card in the corpus. Named strength: the wrestling kayfabe layer maps onto the Epic's actual structure so perfectly it feels inevitable. Named weakness: three description cards (The Steppe, Door Building, The Brickwork) read like stage directions rather than invitations. Table-ready? Yes — this deck runs itself the moment someone picks up Shamash 'The Ref.'
blurb: For anyone who ever suspected the Epic of Gilgamesh was secretly a wrestling event. 54 cards turning ancient Mesopotamia into pure performance — no Akkadian required.

marketingText:
Kayfabizarro: THE URUK RUMBLE – Gilgamesh, Booked as the Original Screwjob (Free Cut & Play Comic Card Game)

The first story humans ever bothered to write down is a grudge match. We just kept the kayfabe.

Four thousand years ago a scribe pressed a reed into wet clay and locked in the booking: a god-king who bullies his own city, a wild man built from scratch to job to him, and a friendship that exists mostly so the crowd has someone to mourn in act three. That is a fight card with a plot. The Epic of Gilgamesh even ships with a continuity error so famous it earned a name. Tablet XII contradicts the eleven tablets in front of it, got bolted on anyway, and stayed in the canon for the rest of recorded history.

This is wrestling for the Bronze Age. Social Story Wrestling: 54 cut-and-play cards that take ancient Mesopotamia, its gods, its monsters, the sacred cedar forest, and the genuinely strange things that happened in the actual myth, and hand them to you as a roster you can shuffle, deal, and perform across a table. No Akkadian required.

WHAT'S INSIDE?
- The Uruk Rumble Core Deck: 54 High-Res "Print, Cut & Play" Cards. You perform HUMBABA "THE JOBBER", the guardian demon of the cedar forest booked to lose so two heroes can look strong; SHAMASH "THE REF", the sun god whose every call lands with a BLOOOM and who is, frankly, the most overpowered official in the history of officiating; and TABLET XII "THE RETCON", the bonus tablet that openly breaks its own story and dares the table to keep playing anyway.
- The Freestyle Rules: The complete Anti-Rulebook. No complicated math, just storytelling, dice-driven chaos, and the Clay-Tablet ruling that makes the table's word as binding as anything pressed into stone.
- The Mortality Engine: the whole deck runs on the world's first recorded fear of death. MORTALITY PHOBIA puts the reaper at your back across the open steppe, MAYFLY PHILOSOPHY orders you to live one day, eat, drink, love, and shut up about it, and THE SLEEP CHALLENGE asks you to earn immortality by refusing to close your eyes. You will lose that one. So did the king.

THE "LIVING DECK" PASS (Free Updates)
The Uruk Rumble is part of the Kayfabizarro historical cycle. Grab it once and every future expansion in the line, more dead empires booked as wrestling territories, lands in your library as a free update. You are not buying a static PDF. You are buying a ringside seat that keeps refilling.

WHY "PAY WHAT YOU WANT"?
The oldest story we have survived because people kept copying it onto fresh clay and passing it down, not because a temple locked it behind a gate. Same plan here. Broke? Enter "0" and take it. Cut it, play it, argue about whether Humbaba deserved better. Want to support the craft? Every dollar goes straight into the next deck in the cycle.

Choose your reality. Become an Epistemic Outlaw.
"The first story ever written was a worked match. You are only the next scribe to book it."
Stay fluffy. — Uncle FrizzleBob
